page.h1: Art auction and estate sale monitoring
page.subtitle: Track Sotheby's, Christie's, Heritage, Bonhams, and regional auction houses for new lots matching your interests.
page.intro: Art collectors, dealers, and researchers watch auction houses on rolling cycles — new lots get cataloged days or weeks before each sale. WebMonitor.fyi monitors auction-house catalog pages for new lots matching artist names, periods, or categories you care about. Results pages get monitored after the sale for hammer-price data.

setup.title: Identify the houses and categories
setup.body: Sotheby's, Christie's, Heritage, Bonhams for international. Regional houses (Phillips, Doyle, Skinner) for narrower coverage.

setup.title: Monitor the upcoming-lots URL per category
setup.body: Each house's upcoming-sales page is filterable by category. Monitor the filtered URL — fewer false alerts.

setup.title: Pre-sale and post-sale monitors
setup.body: Pre-sale catches new lots as they're added. Post-sale captures hammer-price data for record-keeping or appraisal benchmarking.

examples: Collectors watching for works by specific artists
Dealers tracking new inventory and competitor purchases
Appraisers using realized-price data for valuation work
page.limits: Auction monitoring catches what the house publishes publicly. Private sales, pre-auction reserves, and confidential negotiations are outside scope. Some smaller regional houses post less consistently — monitor reliability depends on the house.

faq.q: Can I track sale results to get hammer prices?
faq.a: Yes. Monitor the post-sale results URL for new entries. Useful for tracking realized prices on works comparable to ones you own or are appraising.

faq.q: Does this work for online-only auction platforms?
faq.a: Yes. Sotheby's online sales, Christie's online platform, LiveAuctioneers — all public pages work as monitor URLs.
